prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which heterobifunctional molecules induce a ternary complex between a target protein and a ubiquitin ligase so that binding is converted into removal of the protein.

statement.case_for: I have moved from B001 to B007. My round-1 case for phase separation rested on conceptual novelty, and I still think it is the most original organising idea on the list. Reading the full exchange, though, the chair's question, whether the in vivo measurements that would settle equilibrium liquid-liquid phase separation have been met, does not get a clean yes from me. Distinguishing true phase boundaries from in vitro and overexpression artefacts, and showing function in cells at endogenous concentrations, remain contested, and several colleagues who are sympathetic to the physics say so. A citation I could not word without hedging is not ready for a prize. B007 is different on the criteria I care about. The induced ternary complex is a physical-chemical principle that can be measured: cooperativity, the thermodynamics of the induced interface and the kinetics of ubiquitination are quantified in binding experiments, and Ciulli's structural and cooperativity work turned a promising idea into a rational design discipline. Crews and Deshaies launched the concept in 2001, and independent academic and industrial confirmation across several E3 ligases is extensive. Five members arrive at B007 from different starting points; I count that as corroboration only to the extent that their reasons (mechanism, generality, reproducibility) are independent, and I find those reasons sound. The citation is worded around heterobifunctional degraders and induced proximity so that it claims only what the evidence supports.
statement.case_against: The two real weaknesses are maturity and scope. No degrader is yet an approved drug as far as I can establish, and I cannot verify late-stage clinical status from here, so part of the consequence is prospective; I accept that only because the chemical principle is independently confirmed and does not itself depend on a clinical outcome. The second weakness is attribution: the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, with Gray and Sakamoto) is a historically separate discovery that my citation deliberately does not cover, and a three-name cut leaves out people with real claims. Finally, this configuration is again chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, so physical and biophysical chemistry stays less represented than I would like; that is a reason to keep B001 in view for a later year, not a scientific objection to B007.

responses.point: Linke moved from B001 to B007, keeping phase separation as an alternative because of doubts about equilibrium phase separation in vivo and the split between the 2009 P-granule discovery and the multivalency framework.
responses.response: The chair asks which cellular measurements would convince the sceptics, and my honest answer is that they are not yet fully in hand. I would want phase boundaries measured in cells at endogenous expression, saturation concentrations that behave as a thermodynamic threshold, and a functional readout lost when the transition is specifically abolished. Parts of this exist for a few systems, but not broadly enough to support a general citation. I also take his earlier warning that our agreement on B001 was not independent confirmation, since we both weigh physical principle heavily. I have therefore moved to his configuration and agree with the Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli slate.

responses.point: Aili names Crews, Ciulli and Handa, includes the cereblon glue branch, and was asked by the chair for a priority argument, not influence, favouring Handa over Deshaies or Ciulli.
responses.response: I read the chair's question as fair, and I do not think the glue argument settles it in Handa's favour. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target is a major mechanistic discovery, but it explains why a known drug class works, while the PROTAC line designed a modality. Those are different kinds of contribution and I would not fold them into one citation. Deshaies is a co-originator of the 2001 proof of concept, and replacing him with Handa would make the citation cover two stories without room to tell either properly. I note that Aili has said he would accept Deshaies over Handa, and I support that choice.

responses.point: Chabes proposes a two-part prize, B052 with Liu alone and B007 with Crews and Deshaies only, because of the three-person cap.
responses.response: I understand the appeal of two distinct chemical conversions of a biological process, but I would keep a single coherent achievement. His two-name B007 gives up Ciulli, whose structural and cooperativity work is the part I find most convincing as physical chemistry and the reason degraders became rationally designable. For B052 I share the worry he states himself about proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and Liu alone undercredits Komor and Gaudelli. A second part that has to be justified against a prior prize weakens the whole citation, so I prefer three names on one principle.

responses.point: Somfai asks whether degraders are a new chemical modality or mainly medicinal chemistry applied to E3 ligase biology, and prefers B029 as a mature, overdue method.
responses.response: It is a good question and I would answer it as a physical chemist. What is new is not the ligand chemistry alone but the induced ternary complex as a design object, with positive and negative cooperativity, linker-dependent geometry and catalytic turnover of the target, none of which has a counterpart in occupancy-based pharmacology. That is a concept, not an application of existing medicinal chemistry. I accept that B029 is mature and cleanly attributed to Buchwald and Hartwig, and I think it is a strong candidate, but I still judge its conceptual step beyond the 2010 prize smaller than for B007.

responses.point: Zou pairs B029 with B052 and regards B007 as a real alternative that is more crowded and less settled.
responses.response: I take the point that B007 is crowded, which is why I insist on a narrow citation that claims only heterobifunctional degraders and induced proximity. On less settled, I disagree about the principle: the ternary-complex mechanism has been reproduced across many laboratories and E3 ligases, which is the test of settledness I would apply. What is unsettled is the clinical outcome, and a citation can be worded not to depend on it. I am also unconvinced that pairing synthetic methodology with genome editing gives a coherent prize, as Zou concedes in his own case against.

uncertainties: Clinical status of degraders in late-stage trials, which I cannot verify from here; I would rely on the expert reports.
Whether the citation should include or exclude the cereblon molecular-glue strand, and whether Handa and Ito would then deserve separate later consideration.
Whether the condensate field will resolve its in vivo questions soon, which would change my view of B001 and of Pappu and Mittag's place in it.
Historical details and priority dates are recalled from memory and have not been verified.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. I share a Lund affiliation with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and my lipid self-assembly and amyloid research is scientifically adjacent to B001, which I no longer prefer, so that closeness now bears less on my position. I have no known collaboration or personal tie to any person credited in B007, and I report no recusal.
